assumptions.description: Exactly 3000 exchangeable synthetic adults, unique synthetic IDs, task order and observed=None; no geography, survey weights, missingness or clinical exclusion model.

Supplied CHNS summaries are descriptive calibration inputs from a selected unweighted sample, not population truth. Estimated individual SD is used as a model population SD approximation; marginal estimator uncertainty is unavailable. The supplied regression CR1 intervals are not fitted or treated as independent constraints.

Maximum entropy on ages 35 through 74, matching supplied mean and squared SD, with assumed CDF(38)=0.09, CDF(52)=0.49, CDF(67)=0.89 to locate reported quantiles. Maximum entropy and within-bin probability allocation are assumptions.
Lognormal BMI fitted to supplied arithmetic mean and individual SD. This family, resulting tails, and continuous precision are assumptions; median and q90 need not agree exactly.

Female is Bernoulli at the supplied selected-sample fraction and independent of age, BMI and both biomarkers. No sex coefficient direction is inferred from unresolved external coding. This independence is an unassessed simplification.

A shared two-component lognormal biomarker mixture is a mathematical representation of tail concordance, not a diagnosis. Component membership is independent of age, BMI and sex. One shared fraction and component means/SDs fit two means, SDs and three CDF constraints each approximately. Parameter search bounds and loss scales (mean/SD 0.03; CDF 0.01) are numerical choices, not evidence precision.

Each component has a Gaussian copula for latent age, BMI, glucose and HbA1c. Latent age-BMI correlation is assumed -0.05 and BMI-glucose is assumed 0.20. Remaining correlations solve the supplied three regression projections and Pearson/Spearman functionals analytically. These matrices are one underidentified completion, not recovered participant covariance or causal equations.

External source slopes, correlations, marginals and restored age evidence remain source context; none is forced to equal target estimates. No source-population replay occurred. Shared cohorts, unit conversions and correlated summaries are not independent replications.

Distributional covariance calculations and fixed Gauss-Hermite quadrature are deterministic, not simulated participants. Moment fitting and integration cannot establish generator execution. Individual row randomness does not represent parameter or structural uncertainty.

age_values.derivation: Integer support 35 to 74 inclusive from task.

age_probabilities.derivation: Maximum-entropy exponential tilt on integer support. Formula and exact assumptions in derive_parameters.py; deterministic output in analytic_report.json.

female_probability.derivation: Supplied fraction 0.5368722666264515 used as Bernoulli probability.

high_component_probability.derivation: Joint deterministic least-squares fit of a common class weight to both biomarker margins; not disease prevalence.

glucose_log_parameters.derivation: [mu0,sigma0,mu1,sigma1] for natural log serum glucose, derived by the retained mixture solver.

hba1c_log_parameters.derivation: [mu0,sigma0,mu1,sigma1] for natural log HbA1c percent, derived by the retained mixture solver.

latent_correlations.derivation: Two positive-definite correlation matrices in order age,BMI,glucose,HbA1c. Five unknown entries fitted to the five supplied functionals, two associations assumed. Formula covariance solves preserve the actual distinct adjustment sets; no concatenation of source regression slopes.
